status: Partially fixed — takeover rebuilds successor claim surfaces; aggregate rollback proof remains open
area: Claim identity transitions are not atomic across ledger, runtime lock, direction lock, and admission ticket
finding: Official import and takeover transitions can update only part of the claim identity aggregate. A successful takeover updated the ledger claim and runtime lock actor but retained an expired workAdmissionTicket for the predecessor and emitted a runtime lock without the taskDirectionLock required for scope amendment. Renew resealed the ticket, but could not reconstruct the missing direction-lock authority. The new owner was therefore recognized as active while the public scope-amendment and governed-commit seams still refused it.
expectedBehavior: Every claim identity transition must commit one atomic aggregate: ledger claim, runtime lock, embedded direction lock, work-admission ticket, actor, lane session, lease generation, and authorized scope must either all move to the successor or all remain unchanged. Post-transition validation must fail closed and roll back before success is reported if any identity surface disagrees.
evidenceOrRepro: ATM-GOV-0364 takeover succeeded at 2026-08-13T15:28:27Z, but the retained ticket still named the predecessor and the replacement runtime lock lacked taskDirectionLock. tasks scope add then returned ATM_SCOPE_AMENDMENT_NO_ACTIVE_LOCK, its --claim-first recovery returned ATM_TASK_CLAIM_NOT_READY because the task was already running, and governed commit returned ATM_WORK_ADMISSION_DELIVERY_NOT_AUTHORIZED until tasks renew resealed the ticket. A related forced-import reproduction previously split the ledger leaseId from the runtime lock and dropped the ticket.
followUp: Current source inspection on 2026-09-02 confirms the historical takeover split-brain is partially repaired: `runTasksClaimLifecycle('takeover')` now calls `completeTaskClaimWithWorkAdmission`, the same constructor as an ordinary claim, which creates a successor active claim, lane session, work-admission ticket, actor work session, runtime lock, and taskDirectionLock. It then writes one transition and exposes ticket/direction-lock evidence. This removes the old predecessor-ticket/missing-direction-lock happy-path split. The full expected behavior remains unmet: after `lockStore.acquireLock` succeeds, later ticket/session/direction-lock/transition writes are not wrapped in a rollback transaction, and no injected-failure table test proves all identity surfaces return to their predecessor snapshot. Route import, takeover, renew, and repair through one claim-identity transaction deep module. Add table-driven transition tests that assert aggregate equality and rollback across every surface; do not add command-specific special cases.
